hamster.name: hamster
hamster.intro: Pet hamsters do best on a complete pellet with a small daily portion of fresh food. Below, 68 common foods are rated for hamsters, with portions for Syrian hamsters and stricter notes for diabetes-prone dwarf species.
basics: Base the diet on a hamster pellet. Every piece is the same, so your hamster can’t pick out the sugary bits and leave the fibre, as it can with a muesli-style mix.
Add a small daily portion of vegetables and herbs: about one or two teaspoons in total. Keep fruit to an occasional treat.
Always provide clean, fresh water, ideally from a bottle with a metal spout.
Scatter pellets around the enclosure or bury them in deep bedding, so your hamster can forage and dig as it would naturally.
Hamsters hoard food in their nest. Remove uneaten fresh food every day so nothing spoils in the stash.
Dwarf hamsters (Campbell’s, Winter White and their hybrids) are prone to diabetes, so keep sugary fruit and treats especially small.
Occasional protein treats such as a little boiled egg or a few mealworms are fine.

budgie.name: budgie
budgie.intro: Budgies (budgerigars, often called parakeets in the US) need far more than seed. Below, 68 common foods are rated for budgies, with portions sized for a very small bird.
basics: Make pellets the main food. Veterinary guidance suggests pellets should be roughly 60–80% of a budgie’s diet.

Keep seed to a small part of the diet, never the whole of it. Seeds lack key vitamins, minerals and protein; the RSPCA suggests seed should be no more than about a tenth of the diet for small parrots.
Offer fresh vegetables, greens and some fruit every day, making up about a fifth to a quarter of the diet at most.
Fresh, clean water must be available at all times.
Human food should be plain and tiny: a thumbnail-sized amount for a budgie is like a dinner plate for a person.
When switching a seed-eater to pellets, offer the pellets on their own, not mixed with seed, first thing in the morning when your budgie is hungriest.

cockatiel.name: cockatiel
cockatiel.intro: Cockatiels thrive on pellets and fresh vegetables, and do poorly on seed alone. Below, 68 common foods are rated for cockatiels, with portions sized for a small parrot.
basics: Make pellets the main food. Veterinary guidance suggests about 75–80% of a cockatiel’s diet.
Seed-only diets can lead to ill health and a shorter life. The RSPCA suggests seed should be no more than about a tenth of the diet for small parrots.
Fruits, vegetables and greens should make up no more than about 20–25% of the daily diet.
Cockatiels are vulnerable to vitamin A deficiency and low dietary calcium, so dark leafy greens and orange vegetables are especially useful.
Fresh, clean water must be available at all times.
Human food should be plain and small: about a teaspoon for a cockatiel is like a dinner plate for a person.
